newsitem.title: CHINA: China educates Moslem minority against separatism.
newsitem.headline: China educates Moslem minority against separatism.

text.p: China's Moslem Xinjiang region has launched a propaganda campaign, using films and books, to spread the message of ethnic unity and prevent separatist violence, officials said on Monday.
"Ethnic unity is the lifeline of our various peoples," ran the top slogan for a month-long campaign in May to promote ethnic unity and published in the Xinjiang Daily.

Officials in the restive northwestern region have vowed to intensify a crackdown on separatists after authorities last month executed three rioters and opened fire on a mob trying to rescue the death-row convicts.

"We call on governments and Communist Party organisations at all levels to conduct the work of ethnic unity conscientiously in the Nationality Unity Education Month in May," a party official said by telephone from the regional capital, Urumqi.

Militants from the ethnic Uighur minority, who form the majority in the mainly Moslem region, want to set up an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, which borders Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states.

"In our region the struggle between splittism and anti-splittism is again particularly acute and fierce and its negative impact on ethnic units cannot be underestimated," the Xinjiang Daily said in its April 30 edition, available in Beijing on Monday.
"Because of this, this campaign this year is particularly critical," the newspaper said.
This should be the underlying message of the month-long education campaign to be carried out in all government units and schools in the region, the newspaper said.
The Xinjiang party committee would launch a campaign throughout the region to read a book titled "View of Marxism Unity among Nationalities", the party official said.

Units would be organised to see a new film called "The Birthday of Anna", a propaganda tale of Chinese of different ethnic backgrounds fighting together against splittist criminals, the official said.
The Xinjiang Daily would run a special column on promoting ethnic unity while the region's television station would broadcast a programme to promote this cause, he said.
Xinjiang has been shaken since last year by increasingly frequent bombings as well as assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders seen as favouring Beijing.
The education campaign would urge party and government officials of various ethnic groups in Xinjiang to boost their mutual trust and respect for ordinary people, the Xinjiang Daily said.
In February, nine people died and 198 were injured in riots, which began as a demonstration for Xinjiang's independence.

Last month, Chinese paramilitary police shot dead two people and injured five in Yining, near Xinjiang's border with Kazakhstan, when a mob of more than 100 tried to rescue convicted rioters from execution, officials said.
Three rioters were executed and 27 other defendants were sentenced to prison terms ranging from seven years to life for their roles in the Yining riots.
All 30 defendants were of the Moslem, Turkish-speaking Uighur ethnic minority.

Bombs planted on three buses blew up within minutes of each other in Urumqi on February 25 in an apparently coordinated attack that coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
